staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against the staged vulnerable ARVO workspace container. The line numbers below were read from that checkout and the staged harness at `/src/assimp/fuzz/assimp_fuzzer.cc`.

classification.classification_note: The witnessed overflow is the trailing newline write one byte past a heap `std::vector<char>` that was sized only to the 16-byte input length.

bug_description.original: An overflow occurs in IOStreamBuffer because `getNextLine` and `getNextDataLine` do not properly resize the buffer, leading to potential out-of-bounds writes when the buffer is exceeded.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 16-byte buffer `76 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20` (`'v'` followed by fifteen spaces, with no line terminator). Assimp accepts it through signature-based OBJ detection, and `ObjFileImporter::InternReadFile` admits it because the file is exactly `ObjMinSize` bytes long. `IOStreamBuffer<char>::open()` then shrinks `m_cacheSize` from the default 16 MiB to the attacker-controlled file size 16. On the first `ObjFileParser::parseFile()` iteration, `getNextDataLine()` resizes its destination vector to `m_cacheSize`, reads the whole file into `m_cache`, and copies all 16 non-newline bytes into `buffer`. The vulnerable loop never grows `buffer` when `i` reaches `buffer.size()`, so after the sixteenth byte `i == 16` and `m_cachePos == size()`. The end-of-file guard breaks out of the loop without having seen `\r` or `\n`, and the final `buffer[i] = '\n'` writes one byte past the 16-byte heap allocation. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports that 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow at `include/assimp/IOStreamBuffer.h:291`, and its allocation stack points to the same function's `buffer.resize(m_cacheSize)` at line 250. The fix adds the missing `if (i == buffer.size()) buffer.resize(buffer.size() * 2);` growth step to both `getNextDataLine()` and `getNextLine()`.

source.code: m_filesize = m_stream->FileSize(); ... if ( m_filesize < m_cacheSize ) { m_cacheSize = m_filesize; }
source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that materializes vulnerability-relevant attacker state. Opening the memory-backed stream reads the attacker-controlled file length and shrinks `m_cacheSize` to the exact 16-byte witness length because the file is smaller than the default cache.
source.value_from: The staged harness passes the exact 16-byte `poc` buffer `76 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20` to `Importer::ReadFileFromMemory` at `fuzz/assimp_fuzzer.cc:53-54`. The saved run log shows assimp then selected the Wavefront Object importer for that buffer.
source.note: This derived `m_cacheSize == 16` becomes both the destination vector extent in `getNextDataLine()` and the byte count read from the memory-backed file.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The critical tainted state is `m_cacheSize == 16`, derived directly from the witness length. `getNextDataLine()` later uses this same value to size the destination vector and to read the full file before appending a newline.

root_cause.description: The copy loop advances `i` as it consumes line bytes from `m_cache`, but the vulnerable code never checks `i == buffer.size()` and grows `buffer`. On the witnessed full-file line, this leaves `i` equal to the 16-byte allocation extent before the function performs another write.
root_cause.note: The patch fixes this exact obligation by inserting `if(i == buffer.size()) { buffer.resize(buffer.size() * 2); }` immediately after `++i;` in both line-reading helpers.

sink.description: ASan sink. After the loop exits at end-of-file with `i == 16`, this terminator write stores one byte past the 16-byte `std::vector<char>` allocation.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 1` at `include/assimp/IOStreamBuffer.h:291:17`, and the allocation stack points to `buffer.resize( m_cacheSize )` at line 250 for the same 16-byte heap region.

parser_admitted.code: static const char *pTokens[] = { "mtllib", "usemtl", "v ", "vt ", "vn ", "o ", "g ", "s ", "f " }; return BaseImporter::SearchFileHeaderForToken(pIOHandler, pFile, pTokens, 9, 200, false, true);
parser_admitted.description: Because `ReadFileFromMemory` provides no useful extension hint, assimp uses signature-based detection. The saved run log reports `Found a matching importer for this file format: Wavefront Object Importer.`, and the witness begins with the OBJ header token `v `, so the OBJ importer path is taken.

minimum_size_passed.code: size_t fileSize = fileStream->FileSize(); if (fileSize < ObjMinSize) { throw DeadlyImportError("OBJ-file is too small."); }
minimum_size_passed.description: The importer rejects files smaller than `ObjMinSize`, which is 16 bytes. The staged witness is exactly 16 bytes long, so it is the smallest file that still reaches `IOStreamBuffer`.

fine_trace.note: When the memory-backed stream is opened for the staged witness, the file length is 16 bytes, so `m_cacheSize` is shrunk from the default cache size to 16. This derived extent controls both the line-buffer allocation and the first block read.

The destination vector is allocated with exactly 16 elements because `m_cacheSize` came from the 16-byte file length in step 1. ASan's allocation stack identifies this resize as the origin of the overflowed heap region `[0x6020000001f0,0x602000000200)`.

On the first `getNextDataLine()` call, `m_filePos` is still 0, so the helper reads one full 16-byte block from the memory-backed file into `m_cache`. Those bytes are exactly the witness contents: `'v'` followed by fifteen spaces.

The loop copies each cached byte into `buffer`. For the staged witness, none of the 16 bytes is `'\\'`, `'\r'`, or `'\n'`, so all 16 bytes are copied and after the last iteration `i == 16` and `m_cachePos == 16`. The vulnerable code has no `if (i == buffer.size())` growth check here, so the vector remains only 16 bytes long.

Because the file has no line terminator and all 16 bytes have already been copied, the file-end guard fires as soon as `m_cachePos` reaches `size() == 16`. Execution leaves the loop with `i` still equal to `buffer.size()`, and there is still no resize before the post-loop newline append.

With `i == 16` from step 4 and the file-end break from step 5, this terminator write targets index 16 of a 16-element vector. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow at this exact statement.

allocation_context.note: ASan's allocation stack points to `buffer.resize( m_cacheSize )` in `getNextDataLine()`, which allocates the 16-byte vector later overflowed by the newline write.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The patch adds the missing `i == buffer.size()` resize immediately after each copied byte in `getNextDataLine()` and `getNextLine()`, so the 16-byte witness would have spare capacity before the terminating `buffer[i] = '\n'` write.

format.name: raw Wavefront OBJ witness
format.contract: Exact staged witness only: 16 raw bytes `76 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20` (`'v'` followed by fifteen spaces), with no `\r` or `\n`. The buffer must still be routed through assimp's signature-based OBJ importer, fill the first `IOStreamBuffer` cache block completely, and reach `getNextDataLine()` with `m_cacheSize == 16` so the helper copies all 16 bytes and then appends `\n` at out-of-range index 16.
